messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> P0: kv-cache miss-rate + continuous-batching tail latency spike on prod-us-west-2 (alerts: kvcache.miss_rate > 0.25, batch.lat_p99 > 1200ms)
Dylan: acked. I'm oncall. bringing up dashboard.
Dylan: initial looks: sharp jump in kv-cache key cardinality at 21:07 UTC, simultaneous drop in effective batch sizes (many tiny batches).
Alice: seeing increased funcall errors from feature-service-1: timeouts and 502s to toolgateway. Examples in logs show structured responses with huge arrays.
Ben: stacktrace snippets look like: `ValueError: kv key too long` and `batcher: fragmented batch created (n=1)` recurring.
Dylan: hypothesis: structured tool/function call responses producing large, variable-length arrays causing prefix eviction and huge cache miss churn -> prevents continuous batching from coalescing.
Carla: customer impact? any specific tenants hit?
Alice: two enterprise tenants seeing 5xx rates jump to 3-5% for calls that include toolcall/structured output. Error traces reference `tools.execute` and `serialize_struct_output`.
Dylan: mitigation plan attempt 1: disable prefetch & toolcall-prefetch on router for prod-us-west-2 to reduce cache write amplification. Doing now.
infra-bot: Command executed by Dylan: `POST /admin/route-configs/prod-us-west-2` payload: `{ "prefetch_enabled": false }` -> 200 OK.
Dylan: pushing small change to batcher config: set min_batch_size=4 temporarily so we don't degrade all latency; applying hotpatch.
Carla: can we clamp structured arrays at the runtime serializer to fixed length (like max_items=5) while preserving schema? That would reduce cardinality.
Dylan: yes, there's a quick flag we can toggle: `struct_output.max_array_items`. I'm going to set to 5 in the staging runtime and roll to prod as emergency hotpatch.
Dylan: applying patch via runtime CLI: ```
redwood-runtime patch-config --env prod-us-west-2 --set struct_output.max_array_items=5
```
infra-bot: Patch applied: config version 2026-03-15_hotpatch_214007 - rollout started to prod-us-west-2.
Ben: metrics 2m after toggles: kvcache.miss_rate down from 0.42 -> 0.12, batch.avg_size up from 1.4 -> 3.2, batch.lat_p99 down from 1800ms -> 550ms.
Alice: customers still seeing some truncation-related errors for feature-service-1 where they expect full arrays. Product needs a follow-up on compatibility.
Carla: safe short-term tradeoff. We need a less disruptive long-term fix: either canonicalize toolcall keys (hash only relevant fields) or isolate structured-output routes so they don't write into shared KV cache.
Dylan: I agree. propose next-hotfix: create a routing policy that sends toolcall requests with structured output to a separate cache namespace (or bypass cache) and keep prefix caching for simple calls.
Carla: can you create the routing rule? I can own the follow-up RFC and postmortem.
Dylan: creating routing rule now (prod-us-west-2): tag requests with header `X-StructOutput: true` -> route to `kvcache-structout` namespace.
infra-bot: Route update success: `routes/prod-us-west-2/structured-toolcall` created.
Ben: monitoring: kvcache namespace `kvcache-structout` miss rate stable (no explosion), main cache miss rate steady at 0.08. tail latency further reduced to p99 ~ 320ms.
Carla: writing timeline for handoff: Dylan take initial triage & mitigation, Ben validated metrics, Alice collected customer impact and logs. I'm taking post-incident ownership for RCA + long-term mitigation.
Dylan: handing off to Carla for RCA and customer outreach. I'm staying reachable for escalation.
Alice: customer impact notes: two customers had degraded UX during 21:07-21:27 UTC. Customer-facing ticket IDs: CX-11234, CX-11240. We should offer a brief incident summary and ETA for full fix.
Carla: next steps: (1) RCA on how structured array cardinality mapped to kvcache keys, (2) follow-up PR to serializer to include stable key hashing, (3) change to default runtime to route structured toolcalls to separate namespace, (4) postmortem draft and customer comms. Assigning owners and deadlines.
Dylan: updating incident channel status to "stabilized". Will close pager and set follow-up epic.
incident-bot: Incident set to "stabilized" by Dylan at 2140077800. Pager closed.
Carla: transferring the thread to #postmortems — will attach logs and the quick hotpatch diff: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/hotpatch-214007
Ben: logging note: saved trimmed logs at s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2140076500/ for postmortem.
Dylan: final - thanks all. If anyone sees regression or new spikes, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
